newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normans Wines sees stronger results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normans Wines sees stronger results.

text.p: Australian wine producer Normans Wines Ltd said its results for 1996/97 were expected to be considerably stronger than the A$867,000 loss reported for 1995/96, but it warned it would take time to build its key growth potential.
In the company's annual report, chairman Brian Burns and managing director Rob Byrne said Normans had had a difficult year in 1995/96.
"Results for 1996/97 are expected to be considerably stronger, reflecting increased efficiencies and changed management and marketing strategies which are now flowing through," they said.
The key to Normans' growth now was in value-adding, which was where the profitability lay, they said.
"However it will take time to build the business and that will require patience and perseverence," they said.
Normans said it had set its sights on mergers and acqusitions with other wine companies to boost the company's momentum in the market.
"Our aim is to take the company from a turnover of about A$30 million to A$100 million by the turn of the century and that is an achievable goal," it said.
